# tuitor

> tuitor is a terminal debugger for every language: it records every stop, so you can step back and compare runs. It is a Debug Adapter Protocol (DAP) client that uses the same adapters and the same .vscode/launch.json as VS Code, and debugs PHP (Xdebug), JavaScript and TypeScript (Node.js, Chrome), Go (Delve), C, C++, Rust and Zig (gdb, lldb-dap, CodeLLDB) and Dockerfile builds (BuildKit). One ~9 MB binary, GPLv3 licensed, developed on Linux.

Key facts:
- Install: `cargo install tuitor --locked`, `brew install DorianDevp/tuitor/tuitor`, AUR `tuitor-bin`, `nix run github:DorianDevp/tuitor`. Adapters: `tuitor install <adapter>`, checked by `tuitor doctor`.
- Every stop is recorded; `[` and `]` step back through stops; HISTORY shows every variable at every stop. It does not reverse execution.
- Breakpoint sets: the active set stops the program, other sets record and let it run; COMPARE lines up two runs, also across commits.
- Not supported: `preLaunchTask`, `"console": "integratedTerminal"`, thread list, data breakpoints, memory view. No built-in Python adapter (debugpy can be added in adapters.toml).
- Full docs in one file: https://doriandevp.github.io/tuitor/llms-full.txt
